system.name: Atmosphere
system.one_liner: a formally verified Rust microkernel, proved with Verus, supporting strict isolation for mixed-criticality systems

components.name: A (untrusted)
components.role: an untrusted, unverified container that can perform arbitrary system calls with arbitrary arguments

components.name: T1
components.role: thread in container A; invokes send() to pass a page

components.name: Page
components.role: memory page passed by T1 via send()

components.name: V (verified)
components.role: the single container whose functional correctness is formally proved, mediating between A and B

components.name: T2
components.role: thread in container V; waits on the endpoint and invokes recv() to receive the page

components.name: Receive virtual address
components.role: the virtual address T2 receives via recv(ep, va)

components.name: B (untrusted)
components.role: a second untrusted, unverified container, isolated from A but also able to communicate with V

components.name: Boot (root) container
components.role: outer container from which A, V, and B are established

components.name: Atmosphere microkernel
components.role: the verified microkernel implementing the endpoint-based IPC mechanism underlying send()/recv()

components.name: List of T1's endpoints
components.role: T1's endpoint list inside the microkernel

components.name: Endpoint
components.role: a shared endpoint object referenced by both T1's and T2's endpoint lists

components.name: List of T2's endpoints
components.role: T2's endpoint list inside the microkernel

components.name: List of T3's endpoints
components.role: T3's endpoint list inside the microkernel

content.key_idea: Untrusted containers A and B can only interact through a single verified container V; V's proved functional correctness guarantees isolation and non-interference between A and B even as both exchange pages/endpoints with V via the microkernel's shared endpoint structures.
content.reading_order: Left to right across three sibling containers (A untrusted, V verified, B untrusted) inside a Boot root container; an arrow from V's recv() drops down into the Atmosphere microkernel's endpoint data structures below.

summary: Atmosphere is a formally verified Rust microkernel, built and proved with Verus, supporting strict isolation for mixed-criticality systems. Figure 1 shows its architecture as two rows: on top, three sibling containers - untrusted A, formally verified V, and untrusted B - sit inside an outer 'Boot (root) container', each running one thread (T1, T2, T3); below, a separate 'Containers' row shows the Atmosphere microkernel's internal endpoint data structures (per-thread endpoint lists converging on shared Endpoint cells). The figure illustrates one concrete interaction: T1 in A calls send(ep, va) to pass a Page, while T2 in V, already waiting via recv(ep, va), receives the virtual address; an arrow traces this recv() call down into the microkernel's endpoint lists. The design lets A and B interact only through V, whose proved functional correctness guarantees isolation between them.
summary_zh: 图1示Atmosphere：A(不可信)、V(已验证)、B(不可信)三容器并列于Boot根容器内，各运行一线程；T1经send()传Page，V中T2以recv()接收；箭头指向微内核端点数据结构，示A、B只能经V通信。
notes: layout-proposal: hub-container-over-substrate - a trusted hub container (V) flanked by two untrusted peer containers (A, B) sits above a separate microkernel row exposing the shared endpoint data structures that connect them; 'layered' captures the two-row structure but not the hub-and-spoke trust pattern among the containers.
